resource.name: aws_iam_role_policy
resource.description: Provides an IAM role inline policy. For a given role, this resource is incompatible with using the aws_iam_role resource inline_policy argument. When using that argument and this resource, both will attempt to manage the role's inline policies and Terraform will show a permanent difference. We suggest using jsonencode() or aws_iam_policy_document when assigning a value to policy. They seamlessly translate Terraform language into JSON, enabling you to maintain consistency within your configuration without the need for context switches. Also, you can sidestep potential complications arising from formatting discrepancies, whitespace inconsistencies, and other nuances inherent to JSON.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_iam_role_policy` Terraform resource enables the creation and management of inline policies for IAM roles, allowing fine-grained control over permissions directly associated with a specific role. It is commonly used to define custom access rules for AWS services and resources, such as restricting API actions or enabling service-specific permissions for applications or users. By leveraging tools like `jsonencode()` or `aws_iam_policy_document`, users can efficiently configure and maintain consistent, error-free policy definitions in JSON format, avoiding issues like formatting discrepancies or whitespace errors.

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an `aws_iam_role_policy` resource to attach a JSON-encoded inline policy to an IAM role, granting EC2 permissions (`ec2:Describe*`) with the `policy` argument. It also illustrates the creation of an `aws_iam_role` with an `assume_role_policy` allowing EC2 instances to assume the role, showcasing basic IAM role and policy setup for AWS.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument in the `aws_iam_role_policy` resource allows users to specify a unique identifier for the policy attachment, which can be used to reference or manage the resource programmatically. While optional, setting this argument can help users track and organize IAM role policies within their infrastructure, especially in scenarios involving complex role-policy relationships or automated workflows.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: (Optional) The name of the role policy. If omitted, Terraform will assign a random, unique name.
arguments.llm_summary: The `name` argument in the `aws_iam_role_policy` resource allows users to define a custom, human-readable identifier for the IAM role policy, enabling easier management and recognition of policies within AWS. If omitted, Terraform generates a unique name automatically, making this argument useful for aligning policy naming conventions with organizational standards or workflows.

arguments.name: name_prefix
arguments.description: (Optional) Creates a unique name beginning with the specified prefix. Conflicts with `name`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `name_prefix` argument in the `aws_iam_role_policy` resource allows users to define a unique name for the IAM role policy that begins with a specified prefix, ensuring name uniqueness while avoiding conflicts with the `name` argument. This is particularly useful for dynamically generating policy names in environments where consistent naming conventions or automated workflows are required.

arguments.name: policy
arguments.description: (Required) The inline policy document. This is a JSON formatted string. For more information about building IAM policy documents with Terraform, see the AWS IAM Policy Document Guide
arguments.llm_summary: The `policy` argument in the `aws_iam_role_policy` resource specifies the inline IAM policy document, defined as a JSON-formatted string, that governs permissions and access control for the associated IAM role. By configuring this argument, users can define granular access rules and security policies to manage resource-level actions and permissions within their AWS environment.

arguments.name: role
arguments.description: (Required) The name of the IAM role to attach to the policy.
arguments.llm_summary: The `role` argument in the `aws_iam_role_policy` resource specifies the name of the IAM role to which the policy will be attached, enabling users to define the permissions and access controls associated with that role. By setting this required argument, users ensure the policy is explicitly linked to the intended IAM role, supporting common goals like managing role-based access and enforcing security policies within AWS environments.
